question: A metallic wire having resistivity ρ is cut into four equal parts. The resistivity of each part is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**ρ**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The resistivity (ρ)** of a material is an **intrinsic property **and does not change when the material is cut into smaller parts.
 
• When a metallic wire with resistivity ρ is cut into four equal parts, each part retains the same resistivity of ρ.
 
• Resistivity is **independent of the dimensions of the material**, such as length or cross-sectional area.
 
• Resistivity is dependent on the **material's nature and temperature**, not on its size or shape.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Resistivity (ρ)** is a measure of how strongly a material opposes the flow of electric current.
 
• The formula for resistivity is **ρ = R * (A / L)**, where R is the resistance, A is the cross-sectional area, and L is the length of the material.
 
• When a wire is cut into smaller parts, the length (L) and cross-sectional area (A) may change, but the intrinsic property ρ remains the same.
 
• This concept is crucial in understanding electrical properties of materials and is widely used in designing and analyzing electrical circuits.
